title: Stress-induced despair behavior develops independently of the Ahr-RORgammat axis in CD4 + cells.
authors: Rivet-Noor, Courtney R; Merchak, Andrea R; Li, Sihan; Beiter, Rebecca M; Lee, Sangwoo; Thomas, Jalon Aaron; Fernandez-Castaneda, Anthony; Shin, Jung-Bum; Gaultier, Alban
one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨CD4+细胞中Ahr-RORgammat轴在应激诱导抑郁行为中的作用，属于免疫学与行为学范畴，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Current treatments for major depressive disorder are limited to neuropharmacological approaches and are ineffective for large numbers of patients. Recently, alternative means have been explored to understand the etiology of depression. Specifically, changes in the microbiome and immune system have been observed in both clinical settings and in mouse models. As such, microbial supplements and probiotics have become a target for potential therapeutics. A current hypothesis for the mechanism of action of these supplements is via the aryl hydrocarbon receptor's (Ahr) modulation of the T helper 17 cell (Th17) and T regulatory cell axis. As inflammatory RORgammat + CD4 + Th17 T cells and their primary cytokine IL-17 have been implicated in the development of stress-induced depression, the connection between stress, the Ahr, Th17s and depression remains critical to understanding mood disorders. Here, we utilize genetic knockouts to examine the role of the microbial sensor Ahr in the development of stressinduced despair behavior. We observe an Ahr-independent increase in gut-associated Th17s in stressed mice, indicating that the Ahr is not responsible for this communication. Further, we utilized a CD4-specific RAR Related Orphan Receptor C (Rorc) knockout line to disrupt the production of Th17s. Mice lacking Rorc-produced IL-17 did not show any differences in behavior before or after stress when compared to controls. Finally, we utilize an unsupervised machine learning system to examine minute differences in behavior that could not be observed by traditional behavioral assays. Our data demonstrate that neither CD4 specific Ahr nor Rorc are necessary for the development of stress-induced anxiety- or depressive-like behaviors. These data suggest that research approaches should focus on other sources or sites of IL-17 production in stress-induced depression.
abstract_zh: 目前，重度抑郁症的治疗方法仅限于神经药理学手段，且对大量患者无效。近期，人们探索了其他途径以理解抑郁症的病因。具体而言，在临床环境和小鼠模型中均观察到微生物组和免疫系统的变化。因此，微生物补充剂和益生菌已成为潜在治疗靶点。目前关于这些补充剂作用机制的假说涉及芳香烃受体（aryl hydrocarbon receptor, Ahr）对T辅助17细胞（T helper 17 cell, Th17）和调节性T细胞轴的调节。由于炎症性RORgammat+ CD4+ Th17 T细胞及其主要细胞因子IL-17与应激诱导的抑郁症发展有关，应激、Ahr、Th17和抑郁症之间的联系对于理解情绪障碍仍至关重要。在此，我们利用基因敲除技术来研究微生物传感器Ahr在应激诱导的绝望行为发展中的作用。我们观察到，在应激小鼠中，肠道相关Th17细胞增加且不依赖Ahr，表明Ahr不负责这一通讯过程。此外，我们使用CD4特异性RAR相关孤儿受体C（Rorc）敲除系来破坏Th17的产生。与对照组相比，缺乏Rorc产生的IL-17的小鼠在应激前后行为上未显示任何差异。最后，我们利用无监督机器学习系统来检查传统行为学检测无法观察到的细微行为差异。我们的数据表明，CD4特异性Ahr和Rorc均非应激诱导的焦虑样或抑郁样行为发展所必需。这些数据提示，研究策略应聚焦于应激诱导抑郁症中IL-17产生的其他来源或部位。
